content: In clinical trials, 7% of patients treated with cefotetan experienced no major or minor morbidity, and this result was not statistically significant. Similarly, 6% of patients treated with cefotetan experienced no major or minor morbidity, and this result was also not statistically significant. In studies involving patients with intra-abdominal infections caused by microorganisms from the Bacteroides fragilis group, the eradication rates for isolates at 1 to 2 weeks post-treatment ranged between 70% and 80%. The eradication rates for individual species were as follows: Bacteroides distasonis: 7 out of 10 (70%) Bacteroides fragilis: 26 out of 33 (79%) Bacteroides ovatus: 10 out of 13 (77%) Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron: 13 out of 18 (72%) How Supplied Cefotetan for injection, USP, is provided as a dry white to off-white powder in conventional vials containing cefotetan sodium. The container closure is not made with natural rubber latex. Storage Cefotetan for injection, USP, in its dry state, should be stored at temperatures between 2°C and 25°C (36°F to 77°F). Exposure to temperatures above 50°C should be avoided. The dry material and its solutions may darken depending on storage conditions; however, the product's potency is not adversely affected. Patient Counseling Information Patients should be informed that antibacterial drugs, including cefotetan for injection, are intended solely for the treatment of bacterial infections. They are not effective against viral infections (e.g., the common cold). When prescribed cefotetan for a bacterial infection, patients should be advised to take the medication exactly as directed, even if they feel better early in the course of therapy. Skipping doses or failing to complete the full course of therapy may: 1. Reduce the effectiveness of the immediate treatment. 2. Increase the likelihood of bacteria developing resistance, rendering cefotetan or other antibacterial drugs ineffective in the future. Diarrhea is a common side effect of antibiotics and usually resolves once the antibiotic is discontinued. However, patients may develop watery and bloody stools (with or without stomach cramps and fever) even as late as two or more months after completing the antibiotic course. If this occurs, patients should contact their physician promptly. Precautions with Alcohol The interaction between alcohol and cefotetan sodium has not been established. Patients should consult their doctor regarding the effects of consuming alcohol while taking this medication. Brand Names There is limited information available regarding brand names for cefotetan sodium in the drug label. Look-Alike Drug Names There is limited information available regarding look-alike drug names for cefotetan sodium in the drug label.
